results.title: An important update on our team
highlights:
After months of thinking through how to set Canva up for the next chapter, we have made the incredibly hard decision to make significant changes to how we’re organised, where some of our teams are based, and the roles and skills we need for the future.

This means 1,271 people, or 22% of Canva, will be impacted. For some people, this will mean changes to their roles or being asked to relocate to centralised hubs. Sadly, it will also mean saying goodbye to teammates and friends who have helped build Canva into what it is today.

results.title: Canva | Company Overview & News
results.author: Peter Chawaga Contributor
highlights:
Melanie Perkins—who made Forbes’ World's Richest Self-Made Women List this year—is the CEO and cofounder of Canva, a platform that sees its users whip up 376 designs every second. The $32 billion company was early to generative AI, implementing it in its popular design software, which got a revamp last May. The Australia-based company says its AI tools have been used over 18 billion times since the launch of its Magic Studio launch in 2023. Its customer roster includes T-Mobile, Salesforce, Disney and FedEx—with Canva claiming that over 95% of Fortune 500 companies use its platform. This June, the company—which laid off 10 out of 12 of its technical writers back in April, according to TechCrunch—became the first design platform to find a home in ChatGPT, embedding its creative suite into OpenAI’s personal assistant. It also integrated into Anthropic’s Claude in July and plans to integrate into Salesforce’s Agentforce in the near future. Read Less

results.title: Canva announces major job cuts after 'our hardest year yet'
results.author: Helen Livingstone
highlights:
Canva, one of Australia's best known start-ups, has announced a shake up of the business that will affect 22% of its workers, including job cuts.

In what was "without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history" co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins said 1,271 people would either lose their jobs, be asked to relocate or change roles.

...

The company, which has staff in 37 countries, said Sydney would become the "primary home" for more of its product teams and that as of next year hybrid workers would be expected to spend two to three days in the office.

results.title: Canva lays off over 1,200 people amid slowing growth | TechCrunch
results.author: Ivan Mehta
highlights:
# Canva lays off over 1,200 people amid slowing growth

 Ivan Mehta 

3:59 AM PST · November 4, 2026

Design software maker Canva is cutting 22% of its staff, amounting to 1,271 people, amid a growth slowdown. 

The company’s co-founder and CEO, Melanie Perkins, in a note to employees said while Canva has scaled so far, it needs to change to address slowing growth.

...

Canva is reshuffling its organizational chart and merging its product, growth, and platform teams to reduce communication friction. The company is also reducing “subspecialisation,” which means its employees might be asked to take up more responsibilities. The company is also moving toward hybrid work and asking people to work from an office a few days a week.
